What Is Shepherd Veterinary Software?

Shepherd Veterinary Software positions itself with a refreshingly honest tagline: "PIMS built by a vet who got it." Founded in 2020 and headquartered in the USA, Shepherd was created by a practicing veterinarian who experienced firsthand the frustrations of clunky, overpriced practice management software. That origin story is reflected in every design decision throughout the platform.

Shepherd is a fully cloud-based system designed specifically for small animal, general practice, start-up practices. It is not trying to be everything to everyone. Instead, it focuses on delivering core PIMS functionality with an exceptionally intuitive interface. We found the learning curve to be among the shortest of any system we tested, which is a major advantage for practices that cannot afford weeks of staff training.

At just $99/mo with a per location/month model, Shepherd is one of the most affordable cloud-based PIMS options available. They also offer a 50% discount for new practices, making it an especially attractive choice for veterinarians opening their first clinic.

Key Features

We evaluated every major feature of Shepherd Veterinary Software. Here is a breakdown of what the platform offers.

Intuitive EMR

Clean, distraction-free medical records designed by a veterinarian. Entering SOAP notes and treatment plans feels fast and natural.

Appointment scheduling

A visual scheduling board with drag-and-drop functionality, color-coded appointment types, and multi-provider views.

Client communication

Built-in messaging for appointment reminders, follow-ups, and general client correspondence.

Invoicing

Straightforward invoicing tied directly to treatment plans, with automatic charge capture to reduce missed revenue.

Inventory tracking

Track stock levels, set low-stock alerts, and manage ordering without the complexity of enterprise inventory systems.

Automated reminders

Set up vaccination, wellness, and follow-up reminders that go out automatically based on patient records.

Whiteboard

A real-time hospital whiteboard showing all patients currently in-house, their status, and assigned staff.

Treatment plans

Create and share treatment plans with clients, including cost estimates and procedure details.

Who Should Look Elsewhere?

No software is perfect for every practice. Here are situations where Shepherd Veterinary Software may not be the best fit.

  • Large multi-location hospital groups that need advanced customization, complex workflow engines, and deep enterprise reporting should consider ezyVet or Vetspire instead.
  • Specialty and emergency practices with complex clinical requirements may find Shepherd's feature set too streamlined for their needs. It is purpose-built for general practice, not referral hospitals.
  • Practices that rely heavily on a broad ecosystem of third-party integrations should evaluate whether Shepherd's smaller but growing integration library meets their needs.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Shepherd Veterinary Software cloud-based?
Yes. Shepherd Veterinary Software is a cloud-based platform. You can access it from any device with a web browser and an internet connection. There is no server hardware to purchase or maintain.
Does Shepherd Veterinary Software offer a free trial?
Yes, Shepherd Veterinary Software offers a free trial so you can test the platform before committing. We recommend using the trial period to evaluate the features most important to your practice, such as scheduling, medical records, and any integrations you rely on.
What is Shepherd Veterinary Software's starting price?
Shepherd Veterinary Software starts at $99 per month. The pricing model is per location/month, so your actual cost may vary depending on your practice size and configuration. Contact Shepherd Veterinary Software directly for an exact quote tailored to your needs.
Is Shepherd Veterinary Software good for small practices?
Yes, Shepherd Veterinary Software is well suited for small practices. Its start-up practices, small clinics, solo veterinarians focus means the platform was designed with smaller teams in mind. The interface is straightforward and does not require extensive training.
